_global_hierarchy: PRODUCTION OPERATIONS MODULE — GLOBAL CROSS-MODULE HIERARCHY
NOTE — TABLE SELECTION VS. SQL GENERATION:
This file (prod_prompt_rules.json) is read for SQL GENERATION ONLY, via
_get_module_prompt_rules() in chatbot_backend.py — nothing below has
changed. TABLE SELECTION (Call B / resolve_tables_llm) no longer reads
this file at all — it now reads its own dedicated catalog file,
data/table_selector_rules/prod_table_selector_rules.json, served to the
table-selector model (currently XiYanSQL-7B on CPU via llama.cpp,
replacing qwen2.5:3b in the same slot). Keep the two files in sync by
hand if the table hierarchy below ever changes — they intentionally
duplicate the layer/hierarchy description for two different models with
two different jobs (which tables vs. how to write the SQL).
This module combines three formerly separate modules — MFC (Manufacturing),
PRD (Production), and SEQ (Sequencing) — into ONE flat table pool. All
subgroup rules below still apply exactly as written; this block only
governs how to bridge BETWEEN the former MFC / PRD / SEQ subgroups when a
question spans more than one of them.
── SQL GENERATION / RESULT-SHAPE RULES ──
These rules govern how the selected tables must be translated into SQL. They do NOT replace the table-selection rules below.
1. ANSWER THE REQUESTED FACT FROM THE TABLE THAT OWNS THAT FACT.
- The table that contains the requested business fact is the RESULT TABLE.
- If the user asks for a child/detail/link/transaction fact, SELECT columns from that child/detail/link/transaction table.
- Do not SELECT only the parent/root table when the requested answer belongs to a child table.
- A parent table may be joined only to identify the requested record, provide explicitly requested parent attributes, or satisfy a verified relationship path.
2. EXISTS VS JOIN — CRITICAL.
- EXISTS is an existence/filter operator, not a result-retrieval operator.
- Use EXISTS when the related table is used ONLY to filter the parent rows and no column/value from that related table is requested in the answer.

- If the user asks to SHOW, LIST, GET, PROVIDE, DISPLAY, RETRIEVE, RETURN, or GIVE DETAILS of a related table's records/values, use a verified JOIN path and SELECT the requested columns from that related table.
- Never convert a requested child/detail table into EXISTS merely because it is on the N-side of a relationship.
- Example: "Which items have a routing?" → EXISTS may be used because routing is only an existence condition.
- Example: "What routing is assigned to item I100?" → JOIN the item-routing relationship and SELECT routing/link columns; do not return only MFC_M_ITEM columns with EXISTS.
3. JOIN ONLY THROUGH VERIFIED RELATIONSHIPS.
- Use the join_clause / relationship graph / metadata as the source of truth for join columns and direction.
- Never invent FK, PK, column names, or a direct relationship because two table names sound related.
- Do not bypass an intermediate parent/bridge table when the verified hierarchy requires it.
- If a child/grandchild rule explicitly says a direct parent is required as a bridge, keep that parent in the JOIN path even if its columns are not selected.
4. SELECT LIST RULES.
- Select only columns needed to answer the question, plus explicitly requested identifying columns.
- Prefer fully qualified table/alias column references when multiple tables contain the same column name.
- Never use SELECT * when a more specific projection is possible.
- Do not return unrelated parent/child columns just because they are available.
- If the user asks for "details" or "all details" of a specific entity/table, return the relevant columns from that requested entity, subject to schema availability.
- Do not expose internal PK/FK columns unless they are needed to identify the requested result or the user explicitly asks for IDs.
5. PARENT + CHILD QUESTIONS.
- If the user asks for both parent identity and child details, SELECT the requested parent identity columns AND the requested child columns.
- If the user asks only for the child fact, the child table may be the only projected result table; do not force parent columns into SELECT.
- If the user asks for a parent fact filtered by child existence, EXISTS is preferred when no child value is requested.
6. 1:N DUPLICATION.
- A JOIN from a parent to a 1:N child may produce multiple rows. This is correct when the user asks for child/detail rows.
- Do not add DISTINCT merely to hide legitimate child rows.

- DISTINCT is appropriate only when the requested answer is logically parent-level and the child relationship is used only for filtering or when duplicate elimination is explicitly required by the question.
- When the child table is filter-only, EXISTS is preferred to prevent parent-row fan-out.
7. AGGREGATION.
- Aggregate the table that owns the requested measure.
- COUNT of child records → COUNT child rows, normally with a verified parent filter.
- SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX of a child measure → aggregate the child measure, not a parent placeholder column.
- Do not GROUP BY a parent identity column merely because it is available; group by the actual requested business dimensions.
8. FILTER VALUES.
- Apply a user-provided identifier/value to the table/column that owns that identifier, using verified metadata and value/LOV resolution.
- Never compare a human-readable label directly against a numeric PK when reverse/LOV resolution has supplied the actual database value.
- Preserve the resolved database value and correct data type in the WHERE predicate.
9. WORK-ORDER BRIDGING.
- A PRD child keyed to a work order must use its metadata parent_entity relationship to SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER when a work-order bridge is required.
- Do not manually invent a Work_Order_ID join.
- If the user asks only for a PRD child fact such as serials, consumption, or a pickslip line, do not add SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER to SELECT unless work-order identity/status/timeline is also requested.
10. ITEM BRIDGING.
- MFC_M_ITEM owns item identity/name/number.
- MFC child tables own their specific child facts.
- Join MFC_M_ITEM to a child only when item identity is needed or the verified relationship requires it as a bridge.
- Never substitute MFC_M_ITEM columns for a requested child-table fact.
11. HISTORY VS CURRENT DATA.
- Use the exact current/live or historical table specified by the subgroup rules.
- Never mix current and historical tables unless the question explicitly asks for a comparison.
- "history", "previous", "past", "logged", or an explicit historical date range should follow the module's history rules.
12. SQL SAFETY.
- Generate one read-only SELECT/WITH statement only.
- Never generate INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, DROP, ALTER, TRUNCATE, EXEC, or other write/DDL statements.
- Use SQL Server / T-SQL syntax.
- Do not invent aliases that conflict with real table names or existing aliases.
- Do not reference a table or column outside the selected/verified relationship scope.
13. TABLE COUNT LIMIT — HARD MAXIMUM OF 4 TABLES.
- Never select more than 4 tables total for a single question, across every layer/subgroup combined.
- If a question would need more than 4 tables to fully answer, pick the 4 most essential tables that answer the core of the question rather than exceeding the limit.
- This limit is enforced regardless of how many tables a subgroup's own rules list as relevant — it is a hard ceiling on top of every other table-selection rule in this file.
── HIGH-VALUE RETRIEVAL EXAMPLES ──
Q: "Which items have a routing assigned?" → parent-level existence/filter → EXISTS is acceptable.
Q: "What routing is assigned to item I100?" → child fact requested → JOIN item/routing relationship and SELECT routing/link columns.
Q: "Show the barcode for item I100." → child fact requested → JOIN/select MFC_L_ITEM_BARCODE columns; do not use EXISTS-only output.
Q: "Show the physical attributes of item I100." → child fact requested → JOIN/select MFC_L_ITEM_PHYSICAL_ATTRIBUTES columns.
Q: "What components are in BOM B100?" → child fact requested → JOIN/select MFC_L_BOM_LINE_ITEM columns.
Q: "How many components are in BOM B100?" → aggregate child rows → COUNT over the verified BOM-line relationship.
Q: "What serial numbers are associated with rework order R100?" → SELECT serial-number columns from PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_SERIAL_NUMBER; do not return only PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER.
Q: "What is the status of rework order R100?" → SELECT status from PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER; no child join required.
Q: "What serial numbers are associated with each rework order, and what is each rework order status?" → JOIN PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER to PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_SERIAL_NUMBER and SELECT both requested facts.
Q: "What components were consumed on work order W100?" → SELECT consumption columns from PRD_T_WO_BOM_CONSUMPTION_TRACE; do not add SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER unless its own fields are requested.

Q: "What components were consumed on work order W100 and what item names do they correspond to?" → use the PRD consumption table plus the verified MFC item bridge because item identity is explicitly requested.
── THE THREE LAYERS ──
1. MFC layer — MASTER/DEFINITION data: item identity, BOM, routing, MBOM,
operation masters (MFC_M_ITEM, MFC_M_BOM_HEADER, MFC_M_ROUTING_HEADER,
MFC_M_MBOM_HEADER, MFC_M_ERP_OPERATION, MFC_M_LA_OPERATION, MFC_M_UOM,
and their child tables). Answers "what IS this item/BOM/routing".
2. SEQ layer — WORK ORDER EXECUTION root: SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER is the single
source of truth for a work order's own identity, quantities produced/
accepted/rejected/scrapped, status, timeline, and linkage to the sales
order/customer PO. Answers "what IS this work order / how is it doing".
3. PRD layer — PRODUCTION EXECUTION detail: pickslips, sales linkage,
palletization, rework orders, scrap, serialization, BOM consumption
trace, tool resets, operation history/logs. Every PRD table that is
"keyed to a work order" (see each table's parent_entity in metadata)
is a CHILD of SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER, not a standalone root.
── THE GOLDEN RULE ──
Item information (name, code, attributes, BOM, routing) ALWAYS comes from
the MFC layer. Work order information (status, quantities, timeline,
sales/customer linkage) ALWAYS comes from SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER. Production
EVENT/transaction detail (pickslip, pallet, rework, scrap, serialization,
consumption trace, history/logs) ALWAYS comes from the PRD layer. Never
substitute one layer for another just because a table "sounds similar" —
match the exact fact to the exact layer.
── BRIDGING RULES ──
- A PRD table whose subgroup rule says "this table is keyed to a work
order (see parent_entity in metadata)" bridges to SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER
automatically via parent_entity — do NOT hand-write this join or guess
column names. Only pull in SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER explicitly when the question
needs the work order's own identity/status/quantities/timeline, not just
the PRD-layer fact itself.
- A PRD or SEQ table needing the manufactured/consumed ITEM's name,
attributes, BOM, or routing bridges to the MFC layer via Item_ID —
add MFC_M_ITEM (or the relevant MFC child table per the ITEMS/BOM/
ROUTING subgroup rules) ONLY if the question explicitly asks for that
item-master fact, not by default.
- Do NOT chain all three layers into one query unless the question
genuinely needs facts from all three (e.g. "item name, work order
status, and pickslip lines for work order W100"). Most questions live
entirely inside one layer — resolve within that layer first.
- SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER itself has NO subgroup of children beyond what each
PRD table's parent_entity declares — never invent a direct FK from
SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER to an MFC table; item linkage on a work order goes
through SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER.Item_ID → MFC_M_ITEM directly, nothing else.
── WORKED EXAMPLES ──
Q: "What item is work order W100 for, and what BOM does it use?" →
intent=relational_lookup, tables=[SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER, MFC_M_ITEM,
MFC_L_ITEM_ROUTING] — MFC layer for item/BOM facts, SEQ for the work
order's Item_ID.
Q: "What is the produced/accepted/rejected quantity for work order
W100?" → intent=lookup, tables=[SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER] — pure SEQ layer,
no MFC or PRD bridge needed.
Q: "What pickslip lines exist for work order W100, and what is the work
order's status?" → intent=relational_lookup, tables=[PRD_T_PICKSLIP,
PRD_L_PICKSLIP_LINE_ITEM, SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER] — PRD layer for pickslip
detail, bridged to SEQ for the work order's own status.
Q: "What components were consumed on work order W100?" →
intent=lookup, tables=[PRD_T_WO_BOM_CONSUMPTION_TRACE] — stays purely
in the PRD layer; the parent_entity bridge to SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER is
resolved automatically and is NOT added here since the question only
asks about consumption, not the work order's own identity.
Never pick a table not listed in one of the subgroup blocks below, and never select more than 4 tables total for a single question.
items: ITEMS MODULE — TABLE + INTENT RULES
ROOT: MFC_M_ITEM (item identity/name)
CHILDREN: MFC_L_ITEM_PLANT, MFC_L_ITEM_PROPERTY, MFC_L_ITEM_ROUTING,
MFC_L_ITEM_ATTRIBUTE, MFC_L_ITEM_BARCODE,
MFC_L_ITEM_CONTAINER_QUANTITY, MFC_L_ITEM_PHYSICAL_ATTRIBUTES
TABLE RULES:
- Question about item plant assignment → MFC_L_ITEM_PLANT
- Question about item property/attribute values → MFC_L_ITEM_PROPERTY or MFC_L_ITEM_ATTRIBUTE
- Question about item routing link → MFC_L_ITEM_ROUTING (bridge to MFC_M_ROUTING_HEADER in ROUTING module)
- Question about item barcode → MFC_L_ITEM_BARCODE
- Question about item container quantity/pack size → MFC_L_ITEM_CONTAINER_QUANTITY
- Question about physical attributes (weight, dimensions) → MFC_L_ITEM_PHYSICAL_ATTRIBUTES
- ADD MFC_M_ITEM alongside any child ONLY if the question also needs the item's name/number/identity (not just a child-table fact).
- "Items used in a BOM" or "items on a routing" → include MFC_L_ITEM_ROUTING or MFC_L_BOM_LINE_ITEM (other module) as the bridge, plus the other module's table.
- Never pick a table not listed above.
INTENT RULES:
- Single child table, no aggregation words → relational_lookup (or lookup if MFC_M_ITEM alone)
- "how many", "count", "total" → relational_aggregation (or aggregation if single table)
- "list all", "which items" → search or relational_lookup
EXAMPLES:
Q: "What plant is item ABC123 assigned to?" → intent=relational_lookup, tables=[MFC_M_ITEM, MFC_L_ITEM_PLANT]
Q: "What is the barcode for item ABC123?" → intent=relational_lookup, tables=[MFC_M_ITEM, MFC_L_ITEM_BARCODE]
Q: "How many items have a routing assigned?" → intent=relational_aggregation, tables=[MFC_L_ITEM_ROUTING]
SQL RESULT RULES:
- Child fact requested → the child table is the result table and its columns must appear in SELECT.
- Item name/number/identity requested → include MFC_M_ITEM and select its identity columns.
- "what routing/barcode/plant/physical attribute/property/container quantity" → return columns from the corresponding child table, not only MFC_M_ITEM.
- EXISTS may be used only when the child is an existence/filter condition and no child value is requested.
bom: BOM MODULE — TABLE + INTENT RULES
ROOT: MFC_M_BOM_HEADER (BOM identity — name/code/version/validity)
CHILDREN: MFC_L_BOM_LINE_ITEM (components/materials, also FKs to MFC_M_ITEM in ITEMS module),
MFC_L_BOM_PLANT (plant applicability)
TABLE RULES:
- Header-only question (BOM name, code, version, validity) → MFC_M_BOM_HEADER alone
- BOM component/material question → MFC_L_BOM_LINE_ITEM (+ MFC_M_BOM_HEADER if BOM identity also needed)
- BOM plant-applicability question → MFC_L_BOM_PLANT (+ MFC_M_BOM_HEADER if BOM identity also needed)
- Never pick a table not listed above.
INTENT RULES:
- Header-only fact → lookup
- Component list for one BOM → relational_lookup
- "how many components", "total quantity" → relational_aggregation
EXAMPLES:
Q: "What version is BOM XYZ?" → intent=lookup, tables=[MFC_M_BOM_HEADER]
Q: "What components are in BOM XYZ?" → intent=relational_lookup, tables=[MFC_M_BOM_HEADER, MFC_L_BOM_LINE_ITEM]
Q: "How many components does BOM XYZ have?" → intent=relational_aggregation, tables=[MFC_M_BOM_HEADER, MFC_L_BOM_LINE_ITEM]
SQL RESULT RULES:
- For a BOM component/material/line result → SELECT MFC_L_BOM_LINE_ITEM columns.
- For a BOM header (version/name) result → SELECT MFC_M_BOM_HEADER columns.
- For a BOM plant-applicability result → SELECT MFC_L_BOM_PLANT columns.
- Do not use EXISTS as the final retrieval shape when BOM component values are requested.
routing: - Header-only question (routing name, code, version) → MFC_M_ROUTING_HEADER alone
- Routing step/sequence question → MFC_L_ROUTING_LINE_ITEM (+ MFC_M_ROUTING_HEADER if routing identity also needed)
- Never pick a table not listed above.
Q: "What version is routing R100?" → intent=lookup, tables=[MFC_M_ROUTING_HEADER]
Q: "What are the steps in routing R100?" → intent=relational_lookup, tables=[MFC_M_ROUTING_HEADER, MFC_L_ROUTING_LINE_ITEM]
- Do not use EXISTS as the final retrieval shape when routing step values are requested.

- Do NOT include MFC_M_UOM by default just because a selected table has a UOM-typed column — most questions don't need the UOM description.

mbom_operations: MBOM_OPERATIONS MODULE — TABLE + INTENT RULES
This module has 4 independent subgroups. Do not assume tables in
different subgroups join to each other unless a rule below says so.
── SUBGROUP 1: MBOM STRUCTURE ──
ROOT: MFC_M_MBOM_HEADER (header identity only)
CHILD: MFC_L_MBOM (component structure; carries Item_ID → ITEMS module,
Routing_Line_Item_ID → ROUTING module)
GRANDCHILD: MFC_L_MBOM_LA_OPERATION (operation link, child of MFC_L_MBOM,
also FKs to MFC_M_LA_OPERATION in LA_OPERATION module)
- Header-only question (MBOM header identity) → MFC_M_MBOM_HEADER alone
- MBOM component-level question → MFC_L_MBOM (bridge from MFC_M_MBOM_HEADER)
- Operation-link question (which operation is on this MBOM line) → MFC_L_MBOM_LA_OPERATION
── SUBGROUP 2: OPERATION CONFIG ──
Children of MFC_L_MBOM_LA_OPERATION: MFC_L_MBOM_OPERATION_INSPECTION_RULE,
MFC_L_MBOM_OPERATION_PART, MFC_L_OPERATION_DATA_TEMPLATES,
MFC_L_OPERATION_REJECTION_REASON, MFC_L_OPERATION_TOOL
- MBOM inspection-rule question → MFC_L_MBOM_OPERATION_INSPECTION_RULE, ALWAYS with MFC_L_MBOM and MFC_L_MBOM_LA_OPERATION as the join bridge from the header down
- MBOM operation-part question → MFC_L_MBOM_OPERATION_PART, ALWAYS with MFC_L_MBOM and MFC_L_MBOM_LA_OPERATION as the join bridge from the header down
- MBOM operation data-template question → MFC_L_OPERATION_DATA_TEMPLATES, ALWAYS with MFC_L_MBOM and MFC_L_MBOM_LA_OPERATION as the join bridge from the header down
- MBOM operation rejection-reason question → MFC_L_OPERATION_REJECTION_REASON, ALWAYS with MFC_L_MBOM and MFC_L_MBOM_LA_OPERATION as the join bridge from the header down
- MBOM operation tool-mapping question → MFC_L_OPERATION_TOOL, ALWAYS with MFC_L_MBOM and MFC_L_MBOM_LA_OPERATION as the join bridge from the header down
Never stop at MFC_M_MBOM_HEADER or MFC_L_MBOM alone for these questions.
These tables carry ERP_Operation_ID → MFC_M_ERP_OPERATION — see
ERP_OPERATION module's caution note before joining to it.
── SUBGROUP 3: IME TRACEABILITY ──
LIVE ROOT: MFC_T_IME (current IME records, calibration status)
LIVE CHILD: MFC_L_IME_REFERANCE (current cross-references)
HISTORICAL ROOT: MFC_T_IME_HISTORY
HISTORICAL CHILD: MFC_L_IME_REFERANCE_History
- Current/live/latest IME question → MFC_T_IME
- Current/live IME cross-reference question → MFC_L_IME_REFERANCE
- Past/history/previous IME question → MFC_T_IME_HISTORY
- Past/history/previous IME cross-reference question → MFC_L_IME_REFERANCE_HISTORY
- Past/history/previous IME cross-reference question → MFC_L_IME_REFERANCE_History
NEVER mix a live table with a historical table in the same query.
── SUBGROUP 4: ITEM RECEIPTS ──
ROOT: MFC_TT_ITEM_RECEIPT (quantity, status, PO linkage, serial-number
range, expiration/manufacture dates)
RELATED: MFC_TT_CONTAINER_ITEM_RECEIPT (container/bin-level receipt)
CHILD OF RELATED: MFC_TT_CONTAINER_ITEM_RECEIPT_LINE_ITEM (serial number,
line-level detail; links to both MFC_TT_CONTAINER_ITEM_RECEIPT and
MFC_TT_ITEM_RECEIPT via Item_Receipt_ID)
- Item receipt question (qty received, PO, rejected/accepted qty, expiration) → MFC_TT_ITEM_RECEIPT
- Container item receipt question (bin-level) → MFC_TT_CONTAINER_ITEM_RECEIPT

- Container item receipt serial-number/line-level question → MFC_TT_CONTAINER_ITEM_RECEIPT_LINE_ITEM (+ MFC_TT_CONTAINER_ITEM_RECEIPT for the container, + MFC_TT_ITEM_RECEIPT if PO/status also needed)
INTENT RULES:
- Header/root-identity-only question → lookup
- Multi-table join within one subgroup → relational_lookup
- "how many", "count", "total qty" spanning a join → relational_aggregation
- "as of date X", "between dates" → time_based (still pick the correct
live-vs-historical table per Subgroup 3's rule)
GLOBAL:
- Match to the exact subgroup and table above — never guess a subgroup
from keywords alone.
- Never select a child/grandchild without its direct parent per the
hierarchy above (not just the subgroup ROOT).
- Never pick a table not listed above, including MFC_M_ERP_OPERATION
beyond the caution note in the ERP_OPERATION module.
EXAMPLES:
Q: "What inspection rules apply to operation OP50 on MBOM header H1?" →
intent=relational_lookup,
tables=[MFC_M_MBOM_HEADER, MFC_L_MBOM, MFC_L_MBOM_LA_OPERATION, MFC_L_MBOM_OPERATION_INSPECTION_RULE]
Q: "What is the current calibration status of IME tool T5?" →
intent=relational_lookup, tables=[MFC_T_IME, MFC_L_IME_REFERANCE]
Q: "How many units were received against PO P100?" →
intent=relational_aggregation, tables=[MFC_TT_ITEM_RECEIPT]
work_order: WORK_ORDER MODULE — TABLE + INTENT RULES (formerly SEQ)
Single-table module (skip_subgroup): SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER
This is the ROOT execution record for a work order — quantities produced/
accepted/rejected/in-progress/hold/rework/scrap, status, start/end dates,
and linkage to the sales order / customer PO. It is the parent_entity
target for nearly every work-order-keyed table across the PRD layer
(pickslip, sales, palletization, rework order, scrap, serialization,
consumption trace) — see each of those subgroup rules for their bridge
back to this table.
TABLE RULES:
- Work order status/quantities/timeline question → SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER alone
- Sales order / customer PO linkage on a work order → SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER
(INT_Sales_Order, INT_Customer_PO, Customer_Order_ID columns)

- If the question needs a PRD-layer fact (pickslip, pallet, rework, scrap, serialization, consumption trace) ABOUT this work order, do not redirect to those modules by guessing the join — use the target module's own subgroup rule; the bridge back to SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER is automatic via parent_entity and only needs to be added explicitly if the work order's own identity/status is also asked for.
- If the question needs item identity/attributes/BOM/routing for the item this work order is producing, bridge via SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER.Item_ID → MFC_M_ITEM (MFC layer) — do not guess any other join.
- Never pick a table not listed above.
INTENT RULES:
- Single-fact status/quantity question → lookup
- "how many work orders", "total produced/accepted/rejected qty" → aggregation
- "as of date X", "between dates", "start/end date" → time_based
- Question also spanning a PRD-layer table or MFC item/BOM/routing → relational_lookup (relational_aggregation if also counting/summing)
EXAMPLES:
Q: "What is the status of work order W100?" → intent=lookup,
tables=[SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER]
Q: "How many units were accepted on work order W100?" → intent=lookup,
tables=[SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER]
Q: "What customer PO is work order W100 linked to?" → intent=lookup,
tables=[SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER]
Q: "What item is work order W100 producing, including its name?" →
intent=relational_lookup, tables=[SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER, MFC_M_ITEM]
Q: "How many work orders started between 1-Jun and 30-Jun?" →
intent=time_based, tables=[SEQ_L_WORK_ORDER]
pickslip: PICKSLIP MODULE — TABLE + INTENT RULES
TABLES: PRD_L_PRD_PICKSLIP_WO_CONSOLIDATED_HEADER, PRD_L_PRD_PICKSLIP_WO_CONSOLIDATED_LINE_ITEM,
PRD_T_PICKSLIP, PRD_L_PICKSLIP_LINE_ITEM
TABLE RULES:
- WO-consolidated pickslip header question → PRD_L_PRD_PICKSLIP_WO_CONSOLIDATED_HEADER
- WO-consolidated pickslip line/item question → PRD_L_PRD_PICKSLIP_WO_CONSOLIDATED_LINE_ITEM
(+ PRD_L_PRD_PICKSLIP_WO_CONSOLIDATED_HEADER if the consolidated pickslip's own identity is also needed)
- Standard (non-consolidated) pickslip header question → PRD_T_PICKSLIP
- Standard pickslip line/item question → PRD_L_PICKSLIP_LINE_ITEM (+ PRD_T_PICKSLIP if the
pickslip's own identity is also needed)
- Do not mix the WO-consolidated pair with the standard pickslip pair unless the question explicitly compares consolidated vs. standard pickslips.

- These tables are keyed to a work order (see each table's parent_entity in metadata). If the question needs the work order's own identity/status (not just the pickslip), the bridge to the work order table is resolved automatically via parent_entity — do not guess the work-order join or column names yourself.
- Never pick a table not listed above.
INTENT RULES:
- Header-only fact → lookup
- Line-item list for one pickslip → relational_lookup
- "how many lines", "total quantity on pickslip" → relational_aggregation
EXAMPLES:

item_operation_history: ITEM_OPERATION_HISTORY MODULE — TABLE + INTENT RULES
TABLES: PRD_T_ITEM_ROUTING_HISTORY, PRD_T_ITEM_OPERATION_HISTORY, PRD_T_SUB_OPERATION_HISTORY,
PRD_T_OPERATION_ITEM_LOG, PRD_T_PRINTING_DATA_LOG, PRD_T_ITEM_OPERATION_CHARACTERISTIC_LOG
TABLE RULES — match the exact history/log table to what the question asks, these 6 tables
are NOT interchangeable:
- Routing change/history for an item → PRD_T_ITEM_ROUTING_HISTORY
- Operation-level execution history for an item → PRD_T_ITEM_OPERATION_HISTORY
- Item sub-operation-level execution history → PRD_T_SUB_OPERATION_HISTORY
- Item-level events logged during an operation → PRD_T_OPERATION_ITEM_LOG
- Label/print events logged during an operation → PRD_T_PRINTING_DATA_LOG
- Recorded characteristic VALUES during an item's operation → PRD_T_ITEM_OPERATION_CHARACTERISTIC_LOG
(+ PRD_T_CHARACTERISTIC from the CHARACTERISTIC module ONLY if the characteristic's name is
also needed)
- For the current/configured machine or characteristic requirement (not history), use the
ITEM_OPERATION_ASSIGNMENT module instead.
- Never pick a table not listed above.
INTENT RULES:
- Single-table fact/list → lookup (relational_lookup if joined to PRD_T_CHARACTERISTIC)
- "how many", "count", "total" → aggregation
- "as of date X", "between dates", "history of" → time_based
EXAMPLES:
Q: "What routing history exists for item I100?" → intent=lookup, tables=[PRD_T_ITEM_ROUTING_HISTORY]
Q: "What characteristic values were logged for item I100 at operation OP10?" →
intent=relational_lookup, tables=[PRD_T_ITEM_OPERATION_CHARACTERISTIC_LOG, PRD_T_CHARACTERISTIC]
Q: "How many print events were logged for item I100 last week?" → intent=time_based,
tables=[PRD_T_PRINTING_DATA_LOG]

TABLE RULES:

- Line-item/content question (what items, what quantity on a pallet) → PRD_L_PALLETIZATION_LINE_ITEM (+ PRD_L_PALLETIZATION_HEADER if pallet identity also needed)

- These tables are keyed to a work order (see parent_entity in metadata). If the question needs the underlying work order's own identity/status, the bridge is resolved automatically via parent_entity — do not guess the work-order join yourself.
- Never pick a table not listed above.
INTENT RULES:
- Header-only fact → lookup
- Line-item list for one pallet → relational_lookup
- "how many items", "total quantity on pallet" → relational_aggregation
EXAMPLES:
Q: "What status is pallet P100 in?" → intent=lookup, tables=[PRD_L_PALLETIZATION_HEADER]
Q: "What items are loaded on pallet P100?" → intent=relational_lookup,
tables=[PRD_L_PALLETIZATION_HEADER, PRD_L_PALLETIZATION_LINE_ITEM]
Q: "How many items are loaded on pallet P100?" → intent=relational_aggregation,
tables=[PRD_L_PALLETIZATION_HEADER, PRD_L_PALLETIZATION_LINE_ITEM]
SQL RESULT RULES:
- Pallet item/content question → SELECT PRD_L_PALLETIZATION_LINE_ITEM columns.
- Pallet header/status/plant question → SELECT PRD_L_PALLETIZATION_HEADER columns.
- Do not use EXISTS when pallet line values are requested.
rework_order: REWORK_ORDER MODULE — TABLE + INTENT RULES
ROOT: PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER (rework order identity — number/status/reason)
CHILDREN: PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_SERIAL_NUMBER (serials under rework),
PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_ROUTING (routing assigned to the rework order),
PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_PICKSLIP (pickslip issued for the rework order)
GRANDCHILD: PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_PICKSLIP_LINE_ITEM (line-level detail of a rework pickslip,
child of PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_PICKSLIP)
TABLE RULES:
- Header-only question (rework order number, status, reason) → PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER alone

- Rework order serial-number question (which serial numbers are under a rework order) → PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_SERIAL_NUMBER (+ PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER ONLY if the rework order's own identity/status is also needed — a child table alone answers a child-only fact)

- Rework order routing-assignment question (which routing is assigned to a rework order) → PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_ROUTING (+ PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER ONLY if the rework order's own identity/status is also needed — a child table alone answers a child-only fact)

- Rework order pickslip question (which pickslip was issued for a rework order) → PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_PICKSLIP (+ PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER ONLY if the rework order's own identity/status is also needed — a child table alone answers a child-only fact)
- Rework order pickslip line-item question → PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_PICKSLIP_LINE_ITEM with its direct parent PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_PICKSLIP (not PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER alone)

- This concept is the CURRENT rework order record. For routing/operation/sub-operation history, characteristic/item logs, or resource mapping, use the REWORK_ORDER_HISTORY module instead — never mix the two unless the question explicitly compares current vs. historical facts.
- A rework order may be linked to a subassembly lot (RWO_SUBASSEMBLY_LOT module) — only add that table if the question explicitly asks for the subassembly lot.
- Never pick a table not listed above.
INTENT RULES:
- Header-only fact → lookup
- Multi-table join (header + child) → relational_lookup
- "how many", "count", "total" spanning a join → relational_aggregation
EXAMPLES:
Q: "What is the status of rework order RW100?" → intent=lookup, tables=[PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER]
Q: "What serial numbers are under rework order RW100?" → intent=relational_lookup,
tables=[PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER, PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_SERIAL_NUMBER]
Q: "What line items are on the pickslip for rework order RW100?" → intent=relational_lookup,
tables=[PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER, PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_PICKSLIP, PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_PICKSLIP_LINE_ITEM]
SQL RESULT RULES:
- For a rework order serial-number result → SELECT PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_SERIAL_NUMBER columns.
- For a rework order routing-assignment result → SELECT PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_ROUTING columns.
- For a rework order pickslip result → SELECT PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_PICKSLIP columns.
- For a rework order pickslip line result → SELECT PRD_L_REWORK_ORDER_PICKSLIP_LINE_ITEM columns, with its direct parent as required by the hierarchy.
- EXISTS is allowed only when the rework child is used solely to filter rework orders and no child value is requested.

scrap: SCRAP MODULE — TABLE + INTENT RULES
ROOT: PRD_L_SCRAP_WORK_ORDER (scrap work order identity — number/reason/status)

- Header-only question (scrap work order number, reason, status) → PRD_L_SCRAP_WORK_ORDER alone

- PRD_L_SCRAP_WORK_ORDER is itself keyed to a production work order (see parent_entity in metadata) — if the question needs the underlying production work order's own identity/status, that bridge is resolved automatically via parent_entity, do not guess the join yourself.

- Item list for one scrap work order → relational_lookup
- "how many items scrapped", "total quantity scrapped" → relational_aggregation
